parts.note: an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A clergyman issues a solemn announcement predicting the future.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to say in advance what will happen, a synonym of foretell.

clue.text: Radio he's retuned in old country

indicators.note: a radio retuned has its setting changed, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a wireless set tuned to a station in a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retuned' rearranges the letters of RADIO HES (the apostrophe ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the African state now called Zimbabwe, so it no longer exists as such.

definitions.note: read as 'Adherent is', the 's linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: a pile knocked loose has its parts shifted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A follower's stack of vinyl records gets knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests vinyl, as the surface intends; 'dislodged' scrambles the pile into IPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower of a teacher or cause, the same as an adherent.

indicators.note: something done surprisingly comes out unexpectedly, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat unexpectedly speaks in a way that settles the matter for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the ten letters of VICECONSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusive statement settles a question, leaving nothing further to argue, so it expresses finality.

definitions.note: read as 'Wise Men is', the 's linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical
I is the Roman numeral one, as in number one or first

explanation.surface: The leading journal of the sages, the Wise Men's top publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'first' comes before 'periodical' in the clue, the I goes after MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the three Wise Men who brought gifts to the infant Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew.

clue.text: Be quiet gently going round edge in bright pink

indicators.note: the first pieces go round the outside of the next, enclosing it

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
p, piano, is the musical direction to play softly
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An instruction to hush and move softly around the border of a vivid pink area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' has the hush-plus-softly pair enclosing the edge; 'gently' is the musical direction piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp pink is a bright pinkish shade, named after the colour of cooked shrimps, so shrimp names the colour.

indicators.note: the I comes during the other letters, so it is placed among them
letters jumping about are scrambled, so bungee is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they danced in the middle of a bungee jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges BUNGEE to BEGUNE; 'during' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean ballroom dance in bolero rhythm, made famous by Cole Porter's song.

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a verse is a group of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Returning to the poem with a few more lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse is the back side of a coin or medal, or as a verb to go backwards.

parts.note: cash is money
mere means being nothing more than, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Someone wants only payment, nothing else, in exchange for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine wool from Kashmir goats, and the soft cloth woven from it.

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative, a right-wing British party member
despatched means sent off

explanation.surface: Going along with a Conservative who is being sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to give permission or go along with something, which is to agree.

clue.text: Dispose of one fancy clue, make fun of it

parts.note: to be rid of something is to have disposed of it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter throws out an elaborate clue and mocks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' scrambles the clue into CULE. The closing 'it' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule is to mock or deride, the same as to make fun of someone or something.

clue.text: Like a reminder of a special day

definitions.text: Like a reminder of a special day

parts.words: Like a reminder of a special day
parts.note: special days were once marked in red on calendars, so the clue describes the red ink

explanation.surface: Describing something that brings a memorable occasion to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Saints' days and feasts were printed in red in old calendars; a memorable day is still called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special or memorable one, from the red lettering on church calendars.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means humble or degrading, of low status
a ... as a noun is a domestic servant

explanation.surface: A humble domestic worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Menial describes humble unskilled work, and as a noun names the drudge who does it, a household help.

clue.text: Clothing in which one does not puff so much!

definitions.text: Clothing in which one does not puff so much!

parts.words: Clothing in which one does not puff so much!
parts.note: read the answer as two words: someone who pants less is an under-panter, a comic split of the garment's name

explanation.surface: A joke about garments that leave you less out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNDER PANTS, it means breathes hard too little, the 'puff' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants are a garment worn beneath trousers, the clothing the clue points to.

parts.note: to rattle is to shake noisily
a trap is a device to catch something

explanation.surface: An old banger that shakes and has a faulty door catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a ramshackle old car or carriage that rattles as it goes.

clue.text: During vigil, left less than half a pint

indicators.note: the letters sit within the word vigil, during it

explanation.surface: Someone at a night watch left before drinking even half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is an old measure equal to a quarter of a pint, so well under half of one.

parts.note: ground rent is the earth torn by an earthquake, whose origin lies directly below the point described

explanation.surface: A landlord's charge first levied underneath this property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground rent' looks like a property charge, but means earth split apart; the quake's origin is under this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above where an earthquake starts.

clue.text: Up in Orient travelling? That's rash

indicators.note: Up is placed in the other letters
letters that travel move around, so Orient is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone touring the East breaks out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' tempts as E for East, but 'travelling' scrambles the whole word into ERTION, with 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruption is an outbreak of spots on the skin, which is a rash.

parts.note: opera is plural of opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A melodramatic performance accompanied by a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic behaviour is extravagantly theatrical, as is histrionic behaviour.

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ... was the author of King Solomon's Mines; 'maybe' marks him as one example

explanation.surface: A horseman perhaps who appears worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' seems to be a horseman, but is the first name of the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard describes a drawn, exhausted face, and is also the surname of the adventure novelist Rider Haggard.

clue.text: Thrifty management of nation's resources and finances

definitions.meaning: a country's wealth and its system of production

explanation.surface: Careful running of a country's wealth and money.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means frugality, and also a nation's whole system of wealth and trade.

indicators.note: the work is placed between the letters for the lines

parts.note: Ry is short for railway, the railway lines
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Shoddy work that reads between the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for of poor quality or in poor health.

definitions.meaning: in music a sharp is an ..., a sign altering a note's pitch

explanation.surface: A musician plays a sharp note in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp played' sounds like a wrong note, but a sharp is one kind of musical accidental.
explanation.definitionFit: An accidental is a sharp, flat or natural sign; accidental also means unintentional.

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Something depressing that is partly spiteful too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means dreary and depressing, a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: It may be invisible coming from harbour

definitions.note: an invisible export is a service sold abroad, such as tourism or insurance

parts.note: ex means out of or from
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Something unseen arriving out of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invisible' is an economics term: services such as banking sold abroad are invisible exports.
explanation.definitionFit: Services earned abroad are called invisible exports, as opposed to physical goods.

clue.text: Criminal from Germany full of dread

indicators.note: the outer letters are filled with the inner word

parts.note: angst is anxious dread

explanation.surface: An offender fleeing Germany in a state of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: Angst is the German loanword for anxious dread, apt beside Germany; 'full of' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a gang of violent criminals.

indicators.note: the answer pierces through the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A blade cutting through the skin of a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword, a pointed weapon.

clue.text: Painter perhaps needing energy to become entertainer

parts.note: a painter is one example of an artist
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A painter who needs a burst of vigour to turn performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

parts.note: a battering ram is used to crash through gates
paged means summoned by calling

explanation.surface: A party crasher is summoned and storms around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrasher' suggests an uninvited guest, but here it is a battering ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about wildly, so stormed is a synonym in the past tense.

indicators.note: shot means ruined or worn out, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Men leave after being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but is the noun: edible leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a vegetable eaten for its dark green leaves.
